title: Noise-Tolerant DDoS Detection for Edge Networks
problem: Edge defenders need reliable attack detection when traffic is noisy, attack patterns shift, and compute budgets rule out unnecessarily deep models.
system: A Gaussian shallow neural network injects controlled noise during training to improve robustness without adding inference-time overhead.
evaluation: The study benchmarks the compact model on public and real-world DDoS datasets, including ablations for robustness, convergence, memory, training time, and parameter count.
relevance: A practical path toward low-latency monitoring for edge, IoT, and computational social systems.
imageAlt: DDoS threat model showing an attacker coordinating a botnet while a firewall filters malicious traffic and preserves legitimate clients
figureCaption: Paper figure · DDoS threat model for resource-constrained edge services.

title: Two-Stage DDoS Detection with Language-Model Embeddings
problem: Application-layer attacks can hide signals in textual protocol fields that purely numeric flow models do not capture.
system: Numeric traffic features are fused with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 text embeddings, then passed through two XGBoost stages for detection and attack-family classification.
evaluation: On a curated ML-EdgeIIoT subset, the paper reports 100% accuracy for Normal-versus-DDoS detection and 99.91% for second-stage subclass classification.
relevance: Fine-grained UDP, ICMP, TCP, and HTTP attack labels can support more targeted triage and mitigation in IoT and edge environments.
imageAlt: Two-stage pipeline combining filtered network data, numeric features, MiniLM text embeddings, and two classifiers for DDoS detection and subclass labeling
figureCaption: Paper figure · Numeric and textual features flow through detection and subclassification stages.

title: Foreground-Centric Fine-Grained Recognition
problem: Fine-grained classifiers often learn background shortcuts instead of the subtle subject features that distinguish similar categories.
system: Detected subjects are isolated, standardized, and classified as foreground-centric views so the model attends to diagnostic morphology rather than incidental context.
evaluation: Across visually similar bird species, the paper reports consistent gains in accuracy and per-class reliability, with the largest improvements for confusable categories.
relevance: The same modular strategy can transfer to ecological monitoring, inspection, agriculture, and biomedical imaging.
imageAlt: Foreground-centric recognition workflow from raw bird photographs to isolated subjects, preprocessing, and classification
figureCaption: Paper figure · Field images become standardized subject views before classification.

title: Explainable Arabic Grammatical Error Correction
problem: Arabic error correction needs both accurate edits and feedback that identifies the error type and the evidence behind the correction.
system: MTAGEC unifies correction tokens, error labels, and evidence pointers in a single encoder–decoder sequence-generation architecture.
evaluation: The open-access study builds a 21.8-million-pair synthetic corpus and reports AraT5 F0.5 scores of 80.02 and 81.73 on QALB-2014/2015, plus 69.6% explanation accuracy.
relevance: Joint correction and rationale generation supports more transparent language-learning and writing-assistance systems.
imageAlt: MTAGEC encoder-decoder architecture jointly predicting corrected Arabic tokens, error types, and evidence pointer indices
figureCaption: Open-access paper figure · MTAGEC jointly generates corrections, error labels, and evidence pointers.
